Else all blue-dangerous vertices touch v, yielding a one-centre red avoiding-colouring. Test 1,162 explicit arbitrary graph/target cases with independently enumerated star embeddings.

claims.short_name: Unrestricted graph-host residual-profile mismatch and sharp two-parameter family
claims.claim_text: For all s>=3,t>=4 and positive nonincreasing n,m with b=m1 and N=sum(n)=sum(m2,...,mt), if F(n) and F(m2,...,mt) are nonisomorphic positive-edge star forests, then every finite simple graph simultaneously arrowing both residual pairs has at least 2b+N+1 edges. Sharp family: n=(a,1,1), m=(b,a-1,2,1), a>=3,b>=2a-2, has exact joint minimum J=2b+a+3 over arbitrary simple hosts. The single n311,m5221 instance was already independently established in earlier claim 009 and is not counted as a new discovery.
claims.support_summary: Self-contained unbounded proof: first Ramsey property forces a maximum degree >=b vertex v plus a vertex u of degree >=b after removing v, otherwise explicit red-star colouring defeats it. Second Ramsey condition forces G-{u,v} to contain full F(n) with N edges, yielding e>=2b+N. At equality both hubs have degree b, are nonadjacent, and the residual is exactly F(n). Colouring every edge at u red forces all b+N remaining edges of G-u to form precisely F(m) because its edge count equals M=b+N. Deleting its other degree-b hub v yields F(m_tail), contradicting profile mismatch. Sharp canonical antidiagonal host has weights (b,b,a,2,1). Complete 84630 candidate 15-edge profiles independently checked in Python and C++ by explicit red-hub colouring, plus independent exact integer profile checks. No Lean kernel proof, no global conjecture proof.

claims.short_name: Monotone antidiagonal plateau closure and inherited exact multistar residual cases
claims.claim_text: For arbitrary finite simple host graphs, coordinatewise larger red/blue star targets inherit a proved exact joint-residual value H=J whenever their antidiagonal sum J is unchanged. This closes n=(3,2,1),m=(4,c,d,1) for 1<=d<=min(c,2),1<=c<=3 at J=15; n=(3,2,1),m=(3,2,1,1) at J=13; and infinite families n=(a,2,1),m=(a,2,1,1),a>=4, at J=3a+4 and n=(3,1,1),m=(b,3,2,1),b>=5, at J=2b+6. The parent mathematical proofs remain UNDER_REVIEW and the unrestricted joint residual hypothesis remains OPEN/PARTIAL.
claims.support_summary: Unconditional monotonicity transfer lemma: every larger star forest contains its coordinatewise smaller version, so simultaneous Ramsey arrowing of stronger residual pairs implies arrowing of weaker pairs. As J is coordinatewise nondecreasing and the canonical star-host construction gives H<=J, equality of J along a dominance plateau lifts any established parent H=J. Parent results are the admitted 13-edge, 15-edge rigid cases and two sharp infinite families. Direct explicit antidiagonal algebra proves the listed tail weights; independent source script crosschecks W using two indexings and enumerates nine inherited cases in a declared bounded grid. No new graph enumeration or unrestricted-conjecture proof claimed.

claims.short_name: Exact 15-edge arbitrary-host 322/3111 joint residual by Lovasz factor and deletion
claims.claim_text: Every finite simple G satisfying both G->(F(2,2),F(3,1,1,1)) and G->(F(3,2,2),F(1,1,1)) has at least 15 edges, and F(4,4,3,2,2) attains it. Thus J((3,2,2),(3,1,1,1))=15. This solves one strict-switch 3x4 residual case, not the unrestricted conjecture.
claims.support_summary: Two-vertex deletion forces a ten-vertex full F(3,2,2). A single-vertex deletion forces arrowing (K1,2,F(3,1,1,1)), requiring at least ten edges. The degree-4 case then leaves a ten-edge subcubic residual with <=5 cubic vertices, which the specialized ordinary Lovasz (g,f)-factor matching lemma makes colourable to avoid the residual arrowing. The degree-3 case needs >=8 cubic vertices; handshake plus >=12 nonisolated vertices at 14 edges forces four leaves and a contradiction from deleting a leaf-neighbour and one other vertex. Canonical 15-edge upper forest checked under all 900 arm-colouring classes; no brute-force arbitrary host extrapolation.

claims.short_name: General core transfer and three parity-free infinite original star-forest families
claims.claim_text: Given a source-proved sharp joint residual J=W-(n1+m1-1), the original size Ramsey value equals W when both n1,m1 odd, or W<=D(D+1)/2 for any parity, or W<=D(D+1) if at least one n1,m1 odd, or for opposite-parity leading sizes with 2W<2D^2+R. Combined with source-proved joint residuals, exact original all-host parity-free results are: (a,1,1)/(b,c,1,1) for a>=2,1<=c<=a,b>=a+c-1 at 3b+2a+1; (a,2,1)/(a,1,1,1) for a>=4 at 5a+3; (a,1,1)/(b,a-1,2,1) for a>=3,b>=2a-2 at 3b+2a+2; and five (3,2,1)/(4,c,d,1) original cases at 21.
claims.support_summary: Original vertex deletion forces every G-v to satisfy the two sharp residual relations, hence Delta<=D in any E<=W-1 host. Classical Lovasz degree-core necessity gives >=D+1 saturated vertices for failed cap splits; uniqueness up to 2D+1 saturated vertices forces both caps odd; therefore if at least one cap even failure requires >=2D+2 saturated vertices and E>=D(D+1). Vertex-budget refinement gives 2E>=R+2D^2-2. A (1,2) subcubic matching lemma improves the cubic threshold to nine saturated vertices; isolated odd regular core/exterior avoiding colourings handle b=4,6 and a=4 exceptions; a complete exact 106-class finite degree-two proof handles (211)/(2111). Residual parent results are admitted but still paper-level; full conjecture remains open.
